messages:
Maya K: GlintPay (enterprise) wants a 12mo commit. Peak traffic called out as ~6k req/min for chat (baseline 2k/min) and embeddings batch windows up to ~12k/min for 5-10m. SLA ask: p99 chat <200ms. They returned security checklist (VPC peering, customer KMS, audit retention). Need presales sizing + POC plan.
Aron V: Quick math: assume 6k/min = 100 RPS baseline, 12k/min = 200 RPS burst. For redwood-2-7b q4_0 and avg turn length ~320 tokens we see ~120-140 chat RPS per A100-equivalent GPU with batching + KV cache.
Priya S: Recommendation: reserve a primary chat pool sized for baseline + steady headroom — propose 3 reserved chat GPUs (2 active capacity + 1 hot-standby/cold-warm transition). Separate embed pool: reserve 2 GPUs for embedding batches to avoid contention.
Nina R: Autoscale policy: keep chat pool elastic to add GPUs on short notice and cap at max=6. For embeds, autoscale smaller to max=4 and prefer scheduled preheat for known batch windows.
Aron V: Short rationale: 3 reserved chat GPUs gives predictable latency headroom for sustained baseline + small spikes without immediate scale. Dedicated embed pool (2 reserved) prevents embedding batches from impacting chat p99. Hot-standby reduces cold-start variance for quick failover.
Priya S: Autoscale example (send as sample to customer):
```
metric: chat_rps
scale_up:
  threshold_rps: 140
  add_replicas: 1
  cooldown_seconds: 45
scale_down:
  threshold_rps: 90
  remove_replicas: 1
  cooldown_seconds: 120
max_replicas: 6
```
Nina R: Preheat guidance: schedule a 7-minute prewarm before each known embedding batch window. KV cache warmup + small synthetic warm traffic reduces per-token cost ~20%.
Maya K: Pricing model to propose? They want predictability.
Aron V: Propose 12mo commit covers 3 chat GPUs + 2 embed GPUs at ~35% committed discount. Include burst-credit bucket (e.g., 200 GPU-hours/month) for short-term autoscale and separate on-demand overage rate with higher pricing for persistent overuse.
Priya S: Contract notes: include SLA for p99 latency, a runbook for preheat triggers, and a clause for scheduled batch windows to avoid surprise overage. Offer Private deployment option if they require customer-managed KMS + extended log retention.
SRE-Bot: SOC2 report & security docs: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2.pdf
SRE-Bot: VPC peering guide: https://redwood.example.com/private/vpc-peering
Maya K: Customer requested a 3-day POC next Wed to validate latency and cost. Can SRE support and do we have a test plan?
Nina R: Yes. Plan two lanes: (1) Chat lane: steady baseline + synthetic spikes to verify autoscale and p99; (2) Embed lane: scheduled batch runs with preheat to validate throughput and kv-warm. We'll need an SRE monitor shift and cost telemetry dashboards.
Priya S: I'll draft the POC traffic curves (minute granularity), autoscale knobs, and an acceptance checklist. Aron will own the pricing wording and contract bullets. Maya, please collect the security questionnaire items we can't answer and we'll iterate.
Maya K: Thanks — please post runbook + pricing draft here by Thu EOD so we can send the customer before the POC. :thumbsup:
